tensions.description: Packer's claim of self-defense against Shannon Bell versus coroner reports indicating all five bodies suffered identical blunt force trauma to the head while asleep.
Prosecution assertions that game was abundant and cannibalism was by choice versus Packer's detailed accounts of starvation conditions and extreme winter isolation.
Forensic studies showing potential defensive marks on bones versus bullet fragment evidence supporting Packer's claim that Bell was shot.

Criminal Conviction vs. Forensic Self-Defense Evidence: Packer served seventeen years for murder, yet 1950s forensic matching of bullet lead suggests his account of shooting Shannon Bell in self-defense was accurate.

Grisly Wilderness Tragedy vs. Lighthearted Modern Commercialization: A horrific event involving starvation and cannibalism transformed into collegiate humor, menu items ('Packer Burger'), and musical comedy.
Packer claimed the men died individually over miles and time from starvation/exposure, but all five corpses were discovered together at a single campsite location.
Packer insisted he resorted to cannibalism due to complete desperation in an empty wilderness, whereas local hunters testified large wild game was available in the area.
Packer maintained he acted in self-defense against Shannon Bell, supported by lead bullet evidence, but defensive hacking marks on other victims suggest an active multi-person attack.
Tension between Packer's self-defense and survival narrative versus his legal conviction and denied posthumous pardon based on cannibalism evidence.
